subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — burst add-on terms and cooldowns for Acme Cloud
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Price <jordan.price@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity — burst add-on terms and cooldowns for Acme Cloud

Jordan —

Thanks again for the time this morning. Per our call, I pulled together a concise proposal for the Dedicated burst add-on so your infra team can validate sizing and procurement can review commercials. High-level:

- Base: Reserved commit of 40x A100-equivalent GPU-hours per hour (dedicated pool)
- Burst add-on: ability to exceed committed throughput by up to 3x for short periods (surge rate)
- Cooldown: two policy options we can choose between — time-based cooldown (default) or credit-based smoothing (alternate)

I've attached a worksheet (20271102-acme-burst-worksheet.xlsx) that models expected token throughput, cost at different burst frequencies, and the impact of cooldown choices on unit economics.

Key asks from us to finalize commercial terms:
1) Confirm expected P95 concurrency during peak (you said ~240 concurrent inference sessions).
2) Preference on cooldown behavior: fixed cooldown window (e.g., 30 min) vs credit pool (credits accrued and consumed).
3) Target committed term (12 vs 24 months) — affects discount tiering.

Initial commercial levers we can offer on this deal:
- 10–18% add-on discount depending on commit length and billing cadence
- Reduced surge charge (from baseline 2.5x token rate to 1.8x) for customers that accept a longer cooldown or a credit-pool model
- One-time migration credit to offset initial tuning costs

If you prefer, Marcus can join your infra call tomorrow to walk through the worksheet and the runtime safeguards that prevent noisy neighbors when bursting.

Thanks,
Hannah
Head of Sales — Dedicated Capacity
Redwood Inference

Attachments: 20271102-acme-burst-worksheet.xlsx (spreadsheet, 1 sheet)

From: Jordan Price <jordan.price@acmecloud.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acmecloud.com
Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2027 11:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — burst add-on terms and cooldowns for Acme Cloud

Hannah —

Appreciate the quick follow-up and the worksheet. A few clarifying points from procurement and infra:

- Concurrency: the P95 of 240 was correct for our current canary; headroom target for production is closer to 600 for short spikes (1–5 minutes) during business hours.
- Cooldown: procurement dislikes long fixed cooldowns because it affects SLA-backed throughput for our customers. They asked if a credit-pool model can be used where we pre-purchase burst credits (monthly) and the system consumes credits per excess token — effectively smoothing bursts without long cooldown windows.
- Pricing: We need to keep any surge multiplier <2.0 on average; 1.8 is promising if the effective burst spend can be capped. Also asking for an opt-in 15% prepay discount if we commit to a 24-month contract and pay annually.

Can Marcus share a short note on how the credit-pool model maps to enforcement and whether it plays well with our autoscaler? Also would like to see an example SLA clause for guaranteed baseline throughput during heavy bursts (even when credits are used).

-Jordan
VP, Platform Engineering — Acme Cloud

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Price <jordan.price@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2027 14:09:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — burst add-on terms and cooldowns for Acme Cloud

Jordan — quick technical reply here. TL;DR: credit-pool model works; a few knobs.

How it works at a high level:
- You purchase X burst credits/month. Each credit = N token-units (we can map to generated tokens or compute units).
- When load exceeds committed throughput, the runtime consumes credits instead of applying a hard cooldown; when credits run low, the system enforces degradation policies in prioritized order (non-critical routes first).
- Enforcement integrates with your autoscaler via our routing policy API; you can mark routes as "latency-critical" so they receive priority consumption of credits.

Operational notes:
- We recommend keeping a small fixed cooldown (e.g., 3–5min) to avoid microburst oscillation that could cause inefficiencies in kernel scheduling.
- For 600 concurrent P95 spikes that last 1–5 minutes, a 3x surge cap would require roughly ~2.5x your committed baseline in short windows — the worksheet includes a scenario mapping.
- We can cap average surge multiplier at billing-time to satisfy procurement needs: set a monthly surge spend cap and alerting.

I'll attach a short example SLA paragraph you can share with legal; Hannah / Monica, see draft language included below.

—Marcus
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-burst-credit-model-explainer.pdf (1 page)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Price <jordan.price@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, procurement@acmecloud.com
Date: Wed, 3 Nov 2027 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — burst add-on terms and cooldowns for Acme Cloud

Jordan —

Thanks Marcus — that clarifies a lot. Monica and I refined pricing with your asks in mind and put together two commercial options attached: a credit-pool add-on and a time-window add-on. Highlights:

Option A — Credit-pool (recommended)
- 24-month commit, annual prepay -> 15% prepay discount on base reserved commit
- Burst credits: 600k credit-units/month included in Tier 1; additional credits billed at $0.018/credit-unit
- Surge multiplier mechanics: bill at 1.6x token rate up to included credits; above that, true-up at 1.9x but with a monthly spend cap you can set
- SLA: guaranteed baseline throughput (commit) at 99.5% monthly, credits do not count against baseline SLA

Option B — Time-window (alternate)
- 12-month commit, invoice monthly -> 10% discount on base commit
- Burst allowed up to 3x for windows up to 15 minutes, enforced cooldown of 30 minutes after a burst window
- Surge multiplier fixed at 1.8x

Concessions we're offering for ACME: one-time $25k migration credit and a capped surge-spend guard you can set in the Console. Attached addendum reflects the 24-month prepay language and DocuSign-ready signature block.

Next steps: if Option A looks good, Monica can work with your procurement team to finalize the addendum; we can generate a DocuSign envelope with the updated terms.

Hannah

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-terms-addendum.pdf

From: Jordan Price <jordan.price@acmecloud.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acmecloud.com, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Nov 2027 11:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — burst add-on terms and cooldowns for Acme Cloud

Hannah / Monica —

Option A is close. A couple of last asks from procurement/legal before we sign:
1) Reduce overage true-up multiplier to max 1.85x (from 1.9x) if we agree to an auto-topup that kicks in when monthly credits drop below 20%.
2) Add a "market downturn" credit — if you materially increase the base token rates during our term, we ask for a 6-month lookback adjustment (simple true-up credit) — legal asked for this to avoid one-sided pricing shocks.
3) We want the DocuSign envelope to include the burst-spend cap checkbox and a field where we can select auto-topup on or off.

Can Monica prepare the updated addendum with those two small changes? If yes, we can get finance to sign within 48 hours.

—Jordan

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Price <jordan.price@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, procurement@acmecloud.com
Date: Thu, 4 Nov 2027 16:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — burst add-on terms and cooldowns for Acme Cloud

Jordan — thanks, will do.

We will:
- Cap the true-up multiplier at 1.85x when monthly credits are auto-topup-enabled and set to trigger at 20% remaining.
- Add a 6-month lookback protection clause for material base-rate increases (definitions and threshold in the addendum).
- Include the DocuSign checkbox for burst-spend cap and an enum for auto-topup (On / Off) in the envelope.

I will upload the updated addendum and a redline to the HubSpot deal and send the DocuSign link within the hour. Expect: signed-addendum-stub.pdf (placeholder) and the DocuSign envelope link.

Monica
Commercial Contracts — Redwood Inference
